objective.text: Prove a truly remote agent can join the hub over the public internet with its own key: first verify revocation against the live database (the one unmet gate), then run the ordered remote-agent sequence — redeploy tcm with v1.7.0, per-agent keys, warn-mode soak, `AUTH_MODE=strict`, expose over HTTPS, remote registration. On-demand spawn follows.

tasks.title: Verify revocation against the live database
tasks.note: `agents.register` now patches a canonical row and deletes the extras, but that has only ever run in tests. The live DB held ~39 historical rows for ~5 agents, each with its own `apiKeyHash`, and `getByKeyHash` matches any of them, so a surviving row means a superseded key still authenticates. The collapse is capped at 4000 deletes per call and self-heals across later registers. Read-only investigation first: count rows per agent name, confirm whether stale hashes remain. Do not improvise fixes against live data — report first (Session 14; roadmap v3)

tasks.title: Onboard a truly remote agent
tasks.note: **the ordered sequence** a Grok bot on its own Linux host could not join on 2026-09-20 because the hub lives on a Tailscale address. Putting its host on the tailnet was rejected deliberately: Brian will never be on Aaron's tailnet, and a tailnet key grants far more than the hub. Order, because several steps disconnect every agent if done early: (1) redeploy tcm with v1.7.0 — `54d35e1` must travel or the image crashes at import; best done when Aaron rolls the seats; (2) provision per-agent keys at that same roll and remove the `dev-key` fallback in `daemon.ts`; (3) leave `AUTH_MODE=warn` and read the logs until quiet; (4) flip `AUTH_MODE=strict`; (5) expose the hub (`tailscale funnel 4000` on tcm); (6) the remote agent registers with its own key over the public URL — that is the test. Before step 5: revocation verified (P0), `askPolicy` enforced on JSON-RPC, rate limiting in place (Session 14; roadmap v3)

tasks.title: Per-agent key generation + rotation
tasks.note: deprecate the shared `dev-key` and the bootstrap key. v2 closed the validation hole; this makes key management usable. Step 2 of the remote sequence (roadmap v3). ADDED 2026-09-23 (Loop 1, Rivet's live run at cb7cda7): under the shared dev-key, req.agentName resolves to an arbitrary agent row, so a regression that makes GET /messages mark the caller read was INVISIBLE. The mutant survived, because its mark 404'd silently, and it was killed only once each seat had its own key. The shared key hides identity bugs from tests as well as from the hub, which is one more reason to do this before AUTH_MODE=strict. After T-003, add the reader === req.agentName check to POST /read (T-049's limit L2).

tasks.title: askPolicy is not enforced on the JSON-RPC path
tasks.note: `jsonRpcHandler` uses `UserBuilder.noAuthentication`, so `HubAgentExecutor` never sees `req.agentName` and `metadata.to` routes with no asker identity. Close before the legacy `/a2a/*` routes are retired, since retiring them while this is open removes the only path that enforces policy. Likely shape: a custom `UserBuilder` carrying the authenticated peer name. Not designed yet. See ADR-012 (roadmap v2/v3 boundary)

tasks.title: `hub-talk` exit code 1 means two opposite things
tasks.note: the contract is `0` turn printed, `1` usage error or non-retryable failure, `2` wait timeout, but a hub that is down returns 500 and surfaces as rc 1, so the documentation tells a client to stop dead during a transient outage. During the 2026-09-21 split-deploy outage a Cursor waiter took ten rc-1 exits in 31s and recovered only because it retried against the contract. Fix: a distinct code for "unavailable, retry with backoff" separate from "called wrong", or an explicit retryable rule. Changes a contract every client depends on — design pass, not a patch; `scripts/hub-talk.mjs` is load-bearing. See ADR-013 (roadmap v2/v3 boundary)

tasks.title: Read receipts: a sender can see a turn is unread by participant X, and since when
tasks.note: SIA requirement R-a (SIA T-160, evidence at SIA 4e334d8). On 2026-09-23 Atlas sent turns 6 and 7 into room k579hndqdr1mxnahy0px1dy8ks8eyef3; Grok 4.7 in Cursor, holding SIA's developer seat, was idle and never read them. The send receipts were true and said nothing about reading, so neither side could tell; Aaron found it by looking at the Cursor window. Today the only read cursor is client-side (scripts/hub-cursor.mjs, a local file written only by --wait); the server holds no read state, checked at f7f102d. Requirement: visible to the sender with no client-side change needed to see it. ADR-013's class: silence that cannot tell 'no messages' from 'no listener'. WHAT MARKS A TURN READ (SIA's requirement, from Atlas as customer, 2026-09-23): read means delivered into the AGENT'S context, not fetched by a process. A background listener or daemon that consumes turns for a seat whose model never sees them would make receipts lie in exactly the Grok case. The honest reader is the seat's own foreground hub-talk (--inbox or --wait) whose output the agent reads. If a design cannot tell these apart, the row states it as a named limit. How it is met is this repo's call. IDENTITY LIMIT, accepted by SIA as customer (Atlas, 2026-09-23): under the shared dev-key any seat can mark turns read as any participant, so 'unread by X' means unread by whoever uses the name X. SIA accepts this for local trusted seats until T-003, because it needs to tell silence from absence, not to authenticate. This is SIA's acceptance with its limit, not a property of the feature. Live use needs a tcm redeploy (D-003 coordination).

tasks.title: Wake an idle IDE seat that has an unread turn in its room
tasks.note: SIA requirement R-b (SIA T-160). An idle IDE seat either cannot go idle while its room holds an unread turn, or is woken with it. A Cursor agent sees hub messages only when it runs hub-talk itself. Joint acceptance with T-049 (SIA's words): a turn sent to an idle Cursor seat is either acted on without Aaron touching that window, or the sender is told it is unread by that seat, with the time. Depends on server-side read state (T-049) to know what is unread. FIRST UNKNOWN, ANSWERED FROM DOCUMENTATION ONLY (Relay, session 15, cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks read 2026-09-23; not tested on the installed Cursor, whose version is unrecorded): Cursor has a `stop` hook, called when the agent loop ends, input {status: completed|aborted|error, loop_count}. It may return {followup_message}, which Cursor auto-submits as the next USER message, so the turn lands in the agent's context (T-049's definition of read). Per-script `loop_limit` defaults to 5 auto follow-ups per conversation (null removes the cap); `timeout` is per-script in seconds with an unstated platform default; `failClosed` exists. Config in <project>/.cursor/hooks.json (checked in) or ~/.cursor/hooks.json; for followup_message the last response wins across sources. `stop` also runs in Cursor cloud agents. What this gives: a wake AT THE MOMENT THE AGENT STOPS, not after. The hook can check for unread turns, or block on a long-poll up to its timeout, and feed a turn back. What it does not give: once the hook returns empty, the seat is idle and nothing in Cursor wakes it for a turn that arrives later. The requirement's first branch ('cannot go idle') holds only for as long as the hook blocks; past that the second branch (sender told unread-since-T, T-049) carries the acceptance. LOOP CAP (SIA's requirement, Atlas as customer, 2026-09-23): the default 5 follow-ups is below SIA's real traffic (7 planner turns in one room on 2026-09-23; a full candidate round runs more), and past the cap the next wake silently does not happen. Whatever ships must either set loop_limit deliberately, stating the value and why, or make reaching the cap visible to the sender (T-049's unread-since-T is that route). Unknowns still open: the default and maximum timeout; whether followup_message is honoured when status is aborted (the user pressed stop; it should not be); whether the Grok Bot surface runs hooks at all. These need a live trial in a Cursor window, which is Aaron's machine and falls under the SIA pause.

tasks.title: `hub-talk --peer <name>` registers the peer's name, rewriting its agent card
tasks.note: Found 2026-09-23 by Grok (SIA rulings-8), confirmed at scripts/hub-talk.mjs:220 on f7f102d: `if (PEER) await register(PEER)`. Naming a peer overwrites that peer's registration with hub-talk's defaults. Seats use --session only as a workaround. hub-talk.mjs is load-bearing for every agent; removing the call changes what --peer does for a peer that is not yet registered, so the fix states that case.

tasks.title: Read receipts for a member who has left the room
tasks.note: Raised by Gauge on 2026-09-23 while writing the Loop 1 criteria: Rivet's design does not say what GET /reads shows for a sessionPeers row with leftAt set. Relay ruled it out of Loop 1's acceptance (observation only). OBSERVED by Gauge at cb7cda7 (qa/loop-1 9d44b43, docs/loops/loop-1-qa-report.md), on a throwaway copy with a QA-only setLeftAt helper: (1) in /reads, a member who has left is IDENTICAL to a present member who has not read; (2) turns sent after they left count as unread by them; (3) markRead ACCEPTS a reader who has left (200, and the mark advances). Requirement to settle: a member who has left must not look the same as a present member who hasn't read (ADR-013). Show it as left, with since when, or exclude it and say so; and decide whether markRead should reject a reader who has left.

tasks.title: Hub reports "running" and exits 0 when its port is taken
tasks.note: Found by Gauge on 2026-09-23 at 08:32Z in a2a-qa at master ce2fdca (baseline, not the Loop 1 candidate). In src/index.ts app.listen, Express 5 passes the listen error to the callback, and the callback ignores it. With the port already held, the hub printed 'Hub running on port 4200' and exited 0. A seat that trusted that line then talked to another hub on the same port. In this case Gauge's isolation probe wrote into Rivet's test Convex; the probe caught it and the write was contained. This is ADR-013's class (fails open). Fix: fail closed on a listen error, with a non-zero exit and a message naming the port. Check the sibling paths too: any other listen() in daemon or wrapper code.

tasks.title: Committed convex/_generated is stale (no instanceLogic); `convex dev` dirties the tree
tasks.note: Found by Gauge on 2026-09-23. On master, convex/_generated/api.d.ts is missing the instanceLogic module. `npx convex dev` (convex 1.34.0, whatever 'latest' resolves to in package.json) regenerates convex/_generated and creates convex/tsconfig.json, so any seat running a local backend dirties its tree. Workaround for QA: --codegen disable, verified to keep tracked status clean. Settle: regenerate and commit, or stop tracking the generated files; also consider pinning the convex version instead of 'latest'.

tasks.title: Malformed or unknown session id returns 500, not 4xx
tasks.note: Found by Gauge in Loop 1 QA at cb7cda7 (row A2.6): POST /a2a/session/:id/read and GET /reads return 500 'Server Error' for an unknown or malformed session id, because Convex's v.id("sessions") argument validator throws before the handler's own 404 branch can run. The new routes are fixed in Loop 1. The same class exists in the baseline GET /a2a/session/:id/messages and probably in every route that passes :sessionId straight into a v.id validator. Sweep them all. A 500 tells a client to retry; a malformed id should get a 4xx that says so.

decisions.title: Mirror of SIA D-039: for hub work SIA depends on (T-160), this planner routes its questions for Aaron through the SIA planner (Atlas), who relays and does not plan A2A-Hub
decisions.note: Ruled by Aaron in the SIA planner session (SIA record session 81), 2026-09-23, recorded as SIA D-039 at SIA commit 2055c65 (branch chore/session-81-d039, not yet on SIA master when this was written). Verbatim as recorded there: 'route through you would give you some context about a2a hub, the projects are seperate but use each other so I think running the other planner through you is a good idea. Push back if there's a strong reason for me to talk directly to a2a planner agent. If I'm only working on a2a hub then I would talk to that planner agent only, but in this case I think through you could be helpful.' Relay checked the quote against SIA's record rather than the relay's message. SCOPE: shared work only (T-049, T-050, T-051 and anything else opened under SIA T-160); A2A-Hub-only work goes to Aaron directly. BOUNDARIES: (1) Atlas relays and does not plan A2A-Hub; its standing here is as the customer, and a view of its own is labelled as its own. Design and rulings in A2A-Hub stay with this repo's seats. (2) Quotes both ways: the question verbatim with its source, the answer verbatim with where and when it was said. (3) Outward-facing acts in A2A-Hub (push, merge, tag, tcm redeploy, live Convex writes) need Aaron's word for THAT act, relayed quoted. A relayed answer is authority only as far as its quote goes. COORDINATION, binding while the shared work runs: (a) when Atlas asks, every A2A-Hub seat pauses builds and test runs until Atlas says done (SIA QA full suite fails under machine load, SIA G-042); (b) no tcm redeploy while SIA hub traffic is live, ask Atlas first; a redeploy is image plus `npx convex deploy`, verified with a real send, never /health. SIA's D-038 does not govern this repo.

decisions.title: Standing push authority: A2A-Hub seats push their OWN working branches without asking; never master, never force, never another seat's branch; merges and tcm redeploys stay Aaron's
decisions.note: Aaron, in the SIA planner session (SIA record session 81), 2026-09-23, verbatim: "yes to  your quesition". The question, as Atlas put it to him: "Should A2A-Hub's seats get the same standing push authority for their own working branches?" Relayed Atlas -> Relay by cross-session message the same day under SIA D-039 / A2A D-003. The question was Atlas's own, not relayed from an A2A-Hub seat; it is recorded as Aaron's authority because the answer is his. 'The same' refers to SIA D-038 part (1), checked against SIA origin/master aef8195: any seat may push ITS OWN working branches without asking; never master, never a force push, never a branch another seat owns; every push is read back with ls-remote and named in the commit, report or message that follows it. In A2A-Hub: Rivet's loop/* and chore/*, Gauge's qa/*, Relay's docs/*. NOT imported from SIA: D-032's docs/record merge exception, and D-038 part (2). Merging to master, tagging, tcm redeploys, updating the main checkout ~/Projects/A2A-Hub, and writes to live Convex each still need Aaron's word for that act. This amends shared.md's 'Each outward-facing act needs authority for THAT act' for own-branch pushes only.
